DO NOT DO THIS!

weather_df |>
  pull(tmax) |>
  summary()
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
##  -11.40    7.20   20.60   17.86   28.30   36.70      17

DO THIS INSTEAD FOR SUMMARY TABLES

weather_df |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_tmax = median(tmax, na.rm = TRUE), 
    sd_prcp = sd(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_prcp = quantile(prcp, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

##  4 CentralPark_NY USW00094728 2021-04-28    13  29.4  11.1 2021-04-01         1

# min_rank() gives every tie the same (smallest) value so that c(10, 20, 20, 30) gets ranks c(1, 2, 2, 4). It's the way that ranks are usually computed in sports and is equivalent to rank(ties.method = "min").

lead and lag

weather_df |>
  group_by(name) |>
  mutate(
    lagged_tmax = lag(tmax) # this creates a variable that shows yesterdays tmax, in this case order matters. The lag function does not know the data it just looks at the previous datepoints so need to put in order. 
  ) 
## # A tibble: 2,190 × 8
## # Groups:   name [3]
##    name           id         date        prcp  tmax  tmin month      lagged_tmax
##    <chr>          <chr>      <date>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <date>           <dbl>
##  1 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-01   157   4.4   0.6 2021-01-01        NA  
##  2 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-02    13  10.6   2.2 2021-01-01         4.4
##  3 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-03    56   3.3   1.1 2021-01-01        10.6
##  4 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-04     5   6.1   1.7 2021-01-01         3.3
##  5 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-05     0   5.6   2.2 2021-01-01         6.1
##  6 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-06     0   5     1.1 2021-01-01         5.6
##  7 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-07     0   5    -1   2021-01-01         5  
##  8 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-08     0   2.8  -2.7 2021-01-01         5  
##  9 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-09     0   2.8  -4.3 2021-01-01         2.8
## 10 CentralPark_NY USW000947… 2021-01-10     0   5    -1.6 2021-01-01         2.8
## # ℹ 2,180 more rows
# because we are grouping, when the new group starts it puts NA for the first value instead of taking it from the previous group 
weather_df |>
  group_by(name) |>
  mutate(
    lagged_tmax = lag(tmax), 
    temp_change = tmax - lagged_tmax # this created a new variable with the change in temp each day from the previous day 
  ) |>
  summarize(
    mean_temp_change = mean(temp_change, na.rm = TRUE), 
    sd_temp_change = sd(temp_change, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
## # A tibble: 3 × 3
##   name           mean_temp_change sd_temp_change
##   <chr>                     <dbl>          <dbl>
## 1 CentralPark_NY         0.0115             4.43
## 2 Molokai_HI            -0.000688           1.24
## 3 Waterhole_WA          -0.00155            3.04

Revisit some examples

import, clean, tidy, etc the pulse data, and compute mean and median BDI score at each visit

pulse_df=
  read_sas("data_file/public_pulse_data.sas7bdat") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  pivot_longer(
    bdi_score_bl:bdi_score_12m,
    names_to = "visit", # where should you send the column names
    names_prefix = "bdi_score_",
    values_to = "bdi_score" # where should you send the values, to a column
  ) |> 
  select(id, visit, everything()) |>
  mutate(
    visit = replace(visit, visit == "bl", "00m")
  )

pulse_df |>
group_by(visit) |>
  summarize(
    mean_bdi_score = mean(bdi_score, na.rm = TRUE), 
    median_bdi_score = median(bdi_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
knitr::kable(digit = 2)
visit mean_bdi_score median_bdi_score
00m 7.99 6
01m 6.05 4
06m 5.67 4
12m 6.10 4

in the FAS data, compute mean outcome (ears only) across dose and day of treatment; show in a reader-friendly table

pup_data = 
  read_csv("./data_file/FAS_pups.csv", na = c("NA", "."), skip = 3) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(sex = recode(sex, `1` = "male", `2` = "female")) 
## Rows: 313 Columns: 6
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (1): Litter Number
## dbl (5): Sex, PD ears, PD eyes, PD pivot, PD walk
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
litter_data = 
  read_csv("./data_file/FAS_litters.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  separate(group, into = c("dose", "day_of_tx"), sep = 3)
## Rows: 49 Columns: 8
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (4): Group, Litter Number, GD0 weight, GD18 weight
## dbl (4): GD of Birth, Pups born alive, Pups dead @ birth, Pups survive
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
fas_data = left_join(pup_data, litter_data, by = "litter_number") 

fas_data |> 
  group_by(dose, day_of_tx) |> 
  drop_na(dose) |> 
  summarize(mean_pivot = mean(pd_pivot, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = dose, 
    values_from = mean_pivot) |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by dose and day_of_tx.
## ℹ Output is grouped by dose.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(dose, day_of_tx))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
